title: Source-described thesis, argument, inference step or objection
description: A substantive, correctable account of a thought object. Its identity criterion is distinct from the assertion describing it. Premise and conclusion are roles within a specified step, not intrinsic thesis subclasses. Partial reconstruction is allowed without a claim of logical validity or historical attribution.

proposition.description: The proposition as formulated in this account, including its substantive conditions and negation. It is not asserted true by being recorded.

assertion_force.description: Declared force such as hypothetical, asserted or denied in the account, not the truth or review status of its description.

reconstruction_note.description: What reasoning this account reconstructs and what remains unresolved. Steps and supported theses are separate grounded claims.

coverage.description: Declared coverage of the identified argument, not a proof of completeness, validity or soundness.

transition_account.description: The proposed inferential transition and its limits; premises and conclusions have separate contextual role claims.

reasoning_mode.description: Source-declared mode such as reductio or analogy. Recording a mode neither verifies a rule nor executes a deduction.

challenge_account.description: What is challenged and why; exact target claims distinguish a challenged thesis, inference step, argument or conception. Recording an objection does not accept it.
